thread.title: Representative Alex Burton holds town hall on utility bills - NewsBreak

author: Andrew Newland
title: Representative Alex Burton holds town hall on utility bills - NewsBreak
text:
By Andrew Newland Ann Powell ,
1 hours ago EVANSVILLE, Ind. (WEHT) — Tri-State utility customers say this is one step closer to getting their concerns heard at the state house.
Indiana State Representative Alex Burton returns to his hometown to continue the conversation about utility expenses and what can be done to address it. Aretha Graves says having a discussion with a state representative face to face is a way to get your foot in the door.
“You have concern when your energy bill gets to equal or become bigger than a house payment,” Graves said.
“Every time I go to Indianapolis someone is asking me a question about what is going on in Southern Indiana and I am literally showing them my utility bill and showing them what we are up against,” Burton said.
Representative Burton says he knows the issue all too well. The Evansville resident and former city council man says he’s heard the concerns for years and made it a priority when he became a state rep.
Burton says “We are at a breaking point,” and says lawmakers are slowly making progress to address it. Two weeks ago Indiana Governor Mike Braun named Abby Gray to lead the office of utility consumer counselor.
“The governor has been incredibly strong as it relates to the side of the consumer,” Burton said.
A rate increase for CenterPoint customers was approved last year. Officials decided to phase it in over several years to help minimize the impact on customers. CenterPoint has said there are several ways customers can get help with paying utility bills. But customers and representative Burton says it has not been enough and impacts the economy.
Statement from CenterPoint “CenterPoint Energy is committed to listening to our customers and working with them to prioritize affordability while we continue to provide safe, reliable service to the communities we serve.”
“We have heard our customers’ concerns about energy affordability and the recent rate changes impacting their bills, and we sincerely apologize for the frustration this has caused our customers. We continue constructive dialogue with our customers, community and business leaders and other local stakeholders in southwestern Indiana, including state Rep. Alex Burton, to explore solutions that support those we serve.”
“We are focused on being more proactive in our communications and taking real steps to help stabilize bills and keep energy rates affordable. And, we are exploring additional ways to foster local investment, generate economic growth and support workforce development in southwestern Indiana.”
“We welcome ongoing conversations on these important topics.”
